Section 01

The four pillars

💀

Deliberate Pacing & Real Stakes

The tick is the floor, your hands are the ceiling

Marking a creature starts a 2-second auto-attack tick — a slow, legible metronome that keeps the fight alive without demanding a tap per swing. Everything above that baseline is manual: abilities, footwork, and the shove. Two seconds is deliberately long. It is a rhythm you fight around, not a DPS engine that plays for you. Death removes 10% of experience and half of carried gold.

  • ▸Auto-attack fires every 2000ms on a Marked creature, melee reach only
  • ▸A manual ability resets the tick — skilled play is strictly faster
  • ▸Grid-locked movement at a 205ms base step cadence, slowed by armour
  • ▸Death: −10% XP, −50% carried gold, gold drops on the floor
👁️

Visual Readability Above All

Read the floor, not the monster

Danger is communicated by painting the ground. Every hostile action projects a coloured tile zone with a rising fill-bar showing time-to-impact. Player abilities telegraph identically, so PvP is symmetrical and legible. Silhouettes are chunky, outlined, and colour-coded per faction.

  • ▸100% of incoming damage is floor-telegraphed before it lands
  • ▸Wind-up length scales with damage: 520ms rat → 1150ms wraith
  • ▸Status effects are pips above the head, never buried in a menu
  • ▸One glance rule: a 0.4s glance must convey HP, threat and escape route
📱

Mobile-First, Not Mobile-Ported

Thumbs first, mouse second

The bottom 38% of the screen is thumb territory: floating stick on the left, four 68pt action pads on the right. Everything else lives in the top 25% and fades to 32% opacity after 3.8 seconds of no input, so the world is never occluded during a fight. Desktop gets keyboard parity, never a different game.

  • ▸Minimum 68×68pt touch targets, 10pt gutters
  • ▸HUD auto-dims after 3.8s idle, instant restore on any input
  • ▸Haptics: 14ms tick on hit, 45ms thud on heavy damage, double-pulse on death
  • ▸Safe-area aware; nothing under a notch or home indicator
⚖️

Player-Driven Economy

Every item has a human on both ends

No vendor sells gear. No shop generates items. Every object on the market was pulled off a corpse by a player who risked losing it on the way home. Gold enters through monster drops and leaves through a 5% market tax and death drops — the only two levers we tune against inflation.

  • ▸Zero NPC gear vendors — 100% player-listed supply
  • ▸5% transaction tax is the primary gold sink
  • ▸Death drops re-inject high-value goods into circulation
  • ▸Regional risk maps directly to material scarcity and price floor

Section 02

The core combat loop

Six beats, repeated forever. Exactly one of them is automated — the tick — and everything else is a decision the player has to make with their hands.

01one tap

Mark

Tap the creature. A reticle locks on and an orange arc begins filling. That arc is the 2-second auto-attack tick.

02520–1150ms

Read

The creature swells and the floor it will hit lights up with a rising fill bar. You know the shape and the deadline.

03205ms+/tile

Step, Shove or Commit

Three answers to a telegraph: walk out, shove the creature out (cancelling its wind-up), or eat it behind armour and keep swinging.

04instant

Resolve

Damage pops with the flat armour reduction shown inline — '11 (-6)'. Dodges print grey so a miss is legible too.

0560s window

Claim

Loot scatters across the 3×3 around the corpse, locked to the top damage dealer for 60 seconds. Your filter decides what you even see.

06the long walk

Bank It

Carrying it home is the real risk window — and the only reason the market has supply.

Why the tick is 2 seconds

An earlier draft of this document banned automation outright. Playtesting killed it: on a 6-inch screen, a thumb parked on an attack pad is a thumb that cannot also read the floor, and the player ends up watching their own hands instead of the telegraph.

So baseline damage moved onto a metronome — and the metronome was made deliberately slow. Two seconds is roughly one wind-up window, which means there is always room to act between ticks. The skill ceiling is preserved because any manual ability resets the tick: pressing buttons is always strictly faster than not pressing them. Automation sets the floor. It never touches the ceiling.

The death contract

  • −10% experience. Enough to erase an evening. Never enough to erase a character.
  • −50% carried gold. Banked gold at the Sanctuary is safe. Deciding when to walk home is the risk system.
  • A Remnant spawns. Your dropped gold lands on the floor, locked to you for 60 seconds. Get back inside that window and it is yours. Miss it and it belongs to whoever is standing there.
  • Equipped gear is safe outside Emberfield and the Grey Barrow, which are labelled at the border.

Section 02b

Systems addendum — build 0.9

Five systems added after the first slice review. Each one exists because a specific playtest problem could not be solved with tuning alone.

⏱️

The 2-second tick

Marking a creature starts an auto-attack that lands every 2000ms while you are within melee reach.

The original slice had no automation at all, and playtests showed the obvious mobile problem: keeping a thumb on an attack pad means you cannot also read the floor. The tick solves it by moving the baseline damage off the thumb, and it stays honest by being slow. Two seconds is roughly one telegraph window — you always have time to act between ticks.

  • ▸Melee reach only (1 tile). Out of range, the tick holds at full and fires the instant you close.
  • ▸Any manual ability resets the tick to zero — pressing buttons is always the higher-DPS play.
  • ▸Tick damage = 6 + floor(level × 0.9) + weapon damage.
  • ▸Rendered as a solid arc on the target reticle and a bar on the target plate.
  • ▸Toggleable per account. Off is a valid, higher-skill way to play.
✋

Shove — drag to displace

Hold on an adjacent creature, drag one tile, release. The creature is pushed and its wind-up is cancelled.

Shove is the answer to the 'nowhere to run' problem in a grid game. Instead of only moving yourself, you can move the board. Crucially it interrupts a telegraph in progress, which makes it a defensive cooldown with a positional payoff: shove a Grave Wraith out of its own 3×3 bloom and you have both dodged and repositioned it for a Cleave.

  • ▸Same gesture on both platforms: touch drag, or mouse hold-left-click and release.
  • ▸Exactly 1 tile. Destination must be walkable, unoccupied and not inside the Sanctuary.
  • ▸You must be adjacent to the creature. 2.5s cooldown; creature is braced for 1.2s after.
  • ▸Cancels an in-progress wind-up and deletes the telegraph — the whole reason it exists.
  • ▸A live arrow preview paints the destination cyan (valid) or red (invalid) before you release.
🛡️

Gear slots & flat armour

Eight slots. Armour rating is the sum of equipped pieces and reduces physical damage by a flat value.

Percentage mitigation is unreadable on a phone — nobody computes 23% of 17 mid-telegraph. Flat mitigation is arithmetic a player does automatically: 17 damage against 6 armour is 11, every single time. That predictability is what lets a player decide to eat a hit rather than dodge it, which is the decision that makes armour interesting.

  • ▸Slots: head, neck, chest, weapon, off-hand, legs, feet, ring.
  • ▸damage = max(1, raw − armour). Armour can never fully negate a hit.
  • ▸Damage numbers show the reduction inline: '11 (-6)'.
  • ▸Heavy armour adds encumbrance: +5ms per point to the grid step, capped at +90ms.
  • ▸Ember Plate is 12 armour and 8 encumbrance — best mitigation, worst footwork.
✦

Loot: spread, claim, filter

Drops scatter over 1 sqm, lock to the top damage dealer for 60 seconds, and are hidden entirely if your filter excludes them.

Three separate problems solved by three separate rules. Spread stops a nine-item drop becoming an unreadable pile on one 44px tile. The 60-second claim stops the highest-level player in the zone from stealing every kill they did not earn. The filter is the mobile clarity valve: if you are farming Grave Silk, sewer pelts should not be drawn on your screen at all.

  • ▸Drops distribute across the walkable 3×3 around the corpse, corpse tile first.
  • ▸Top damage dealer holds an exclusive 60s claim; a lock icon and countdown arc render on the stack.
  • ▸After 60s the stack is free for anyone. Ground items decay after 3 minutes.
  • ▸Filtered-out items are not drawn, not tappable, and skipped by auto pick-up.
  • ▸Auto pick-up takes claimable, filtered loot the moment you step onto its tile.
🕊️

Protected zones

Inside a Protected Zone creatures cannot land damage and PvP is hard-blocked. You may still attack out.

The Sanctuary is the only place in the world where the risk system switches off, and it has to be absolute: any ambiguity about whether you are safe makes banking loot feel like a gamble rather than a reward. Note the deliberate asymmetry requested for the slice — you can attack out of a PZ but nothing can attack in.

  • ▸Creatures may not path into a PZ and may not resolve damage against a player inside one.
  • ▸PvP attacks are rejected outright inside a PZ. No exceptions, no flagging.
  • ▸You may attack creatures standing outside the PZ from within it.
  • ▸Shoving a creature into a PZ is blocked — otherwise it becomes an untouchable-mob exploit.
  • ▸The zone border is drawn as a dashed gold ring, labelled, and shown on the HUD.

Known open issues these rules create

A design bible that only lists wins is a sales deck. These are live and unresolved.

PZ safe-spotting is currently exploitable

Attack-out / no-attack-in means a player can stand on the Sanctuary border and freely kill anything that wanders adjacent. Shipping mitigation: creatures leash and disengage after 4 seconds of being unable to reach their attacker, and regenerate to full. Implemented in the slice: creatures will not path adjacent to the PZ, and cannot be shoved into it.

Auto-attack weakens the anti-bot argument

A 2s tick is trivially automatable, so combat is no longer inherently bot-hostile. The load moves to telegraph dodging and shove usage — telemetry now flags accounts with abnormally low damage-taken-per-hour alongside high tick counts.

Loot filters hide items from the economy

If most players filter out common materials, those materials stop entering the market and low-level crafting stalls. We watch the ratio of dropped-to-collected per item and adjust drop rates, not filters — the filter must stay a pure player-clarity tool.

Haptic language

  • 8ms tick — target acquired, ability on cooldown (rejection)
  • 14ms tap — you land a hit
  • 45ms thud — you take >15 damage
  • 12/30/18 triple — kill confirmed
  • 26/20/12 decay — shove connects
  • 90/60/140 double-thud — death

Haptics are never decorative. If it buzzes, world state changed.

Section 04

Telegraphing & the bestiary

Every enemy is defined first by its tell, second by its numbers. If a designer cannot describe the tell in one sentence, the monster does not ship.

🐀

Hollow Rat

26 hp · 6 dmg · 12 xp

520ms tell

Tell — Rears up on hind legs — one tile of orange floor.

Swarms. Individually trivial, lethal in fours because each one resets your step timer.

🕷️

Cave Spider

54 hp · 11 dmg · 34 xp

700ms tell

Tell — Fangs flare violet — applies POISON, a 3-tick DOT shown as green pips.

Fast mover, slow attacker. Punishes players who stand still to heal.

🔥

Ember Husk

88 hp · 17 dmg · 70 xp

950ms tell

Tell — Telegraphs a 3-tile line of glowing floor. Sidestep, do not outrun.

Ranged zoner. Teaches the core lesson: read the floor, not the monster.

👻

Grave Wraith

150 hp · 26 dmg · 165 xp

1150ms tell

Tell — Screams and paints a 3x3 cyan bloom. Full 1.15s to leave the zone.

Territory boss of the Barrow. Solo-able at level 8 with perfect footwork, never before.

Player kit — four buttons, four decisions

⚔️

Strike

8 mana · 0.8s cd

Manual melee swing on the targeted adjacent tile. Costs mana — the 2s tick is the free baseline, Strike is the burst.

Strike used to be free and spammable, which made the 2-second tick pointless: optimal play was hammering one button. The 8-mana price restores the intended rhythm — free metronome damage plus deliberate, mana-gated bursts — and gives Blue Draughts a job in every fight, not just mage fights.

🌀

Cleave

14 mana · 4.2s cd

Hits every enemy in the 8 tiles around you after a 0.42s wind-up.

Your own wind-up is telegraphed to other players too. Committing to Cleave is a readable, punishable choice — symmetry with monster tells.

✨

Ash Bolt

20 mana · 2.6s cd

Straight-line projectile, 5 tiles, stops on the first target.

The only reliable way to open on an Ember Husk before it zones you. Mana-gated so it can never become the default attack.

🛡️

Ward

26 mana · 9.0s cd

Absorbs the next 45 damage for 6 seconds. Consumes a full thumb-press.

Defensive cooldowns are held, not spammed. Long CD + visible bubble = other players can count your Ward down out loud.

Section 05

World structure & risk gradient

One contiguous 40×40 grid, no loading screens, no instances. Risk rises as you walk north. The single Sanctuary sits at the southern tip, which means every trip home is a decision.

The Grey Barrow

Lv 9+ · Deep world, no respawn shrine

Spawns: Grave Wraith, Ember Husk · tiles 40×11

risk

Emberfield

Lv 6–9 · Full loot on death

Spawns: Ember Husk, Cave Spider · tiles 18×11

risk

The Weeping Webs

Lv 3–6 · Contested

Spawns: Cave Spider, Hollow Rat · tiles 22×11

risk

Ashfall Hollow

Lv 1–3 · Safe-adjacent

Spawns: Hollow Rat · tiles 40×18

risk

Section 06

Economy design

Faucets

  • —Monster gold drops (1–90 per kill, region-scaled)
  • —Material drops with hard rarity gates
  • —Unclaimed Remnants decaying back into the world

Sinks

  • —5% market transaction tax (burned)
  • —50% carried gold destroyed on death
  • —Consumables: salves and draughts are never refundable

Levers we will pull

  • —Region respawn density (supply)
  • —Rarity table weights (scarcity)
  • —Tax rate, 3%–8% band (velocity)
  • —Barrow seasonal reset (shock absorber)

The one rule

No item enters the world except through a player killing something and physically carrying it home. Monetisation touches cosmetics only — the moment gold or gear can be bought, the risk system that makes the walk home meaningful becomes optional, and the entire design collapses.

Section 07

Risk register & roadmap

Resolved

Manual combat feels like work on a 6-inch screen

Resolved by the 2s auto-attack tick: baseline damage no longer requires a thumb, freeing the player to read telegraphs. Abilities remain manual on 68pt pads with haptic confirmation, and resetting the tick rewards active play without punishing passive play.

Medium

Heavy armour becomes mandatory and flattens build variety

Encumbrance is the counterweight: +5ms per point of step time, capped at +90ms. In the Grey Barrow, where every wraith telegraphs a 3×3, a +40ms step is measurably worse than 12 points of mitigation. Light builds win in high-telegraph zones, heavy builds win in swarm zones.

High

Full-loot death drives away casual players

Remnants uses partial loss: XP and carried gold only, never equipped gear — except in Emberfield and the Grey Barrow, which are opt-in and clearly labelled at the region border.

Medium

Player economy collapses from bot farming

Manual-input combat is inherently bot-hostile: telegraph dodging requires reactive play. Telemetry flags perfect-dodge-rate outliers automatically.

Medium

Telegraph spam becomes visual noise in group fights

Max 3 concurrent zones rendered per tile; overlapping zones merge to the highest-damage colour. Player-cast telegraphs render at 60% alpha of hostile ones.
